questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: A tree has 8 vertices. How many edges does it have?
questions.explanation: Every tree on n vertices has exactly n-1 edges, here 7. Adding one more edge would create a cycle, contradicting that a tree is acyclic.
questions.hint: A tree on n vertices has n minus 1 edges.

questions.stem: How many labeled trees exist on 8 vertices? (case 3)
questions.explanation: By Cayley's formula there are n^(n-2) labeled trees on n vertices, giving 262144 for n=8. This counts distinct labelings, not just unlabeled shapes.
questions.hint: Use Cayley formula n to the power n minus 2.
